body_md: Vite loads wasm-pack output as an ES module. Put pkg in deps, `import init from './pkg/app.js'`, and call `await init()` before exports. HMR keeps Rust state while JS reloads around it.

quiz.explain: Vite serves .wasm with correct MIME and bundles the glue.
options: Import glue JS and await init before use
quiz.q: How do you wire wasm-pack output into Vite?

takeaway: Import glue, initialize once, then call exports.
trap: Calling exports before init resolves causes null traps.

body_md: `wasm-opt -Oz` shrinks binaries by inlining, DCE, and simplifying. Run it after wasm-pack or enable in CI. Measure before and after; -Oz trades tiny speed for smallest bytes.

quiz.explain: Binaryen optimizer removes dead code and folds constants.

takeaway: Optimize for size before measuring budgets.
trap: Running -O4 blindly when -Oz fits caching better.

body_md: wee_alloc is a tiny allocator for wasm, replacing dlmalloc to save kilobytes. Add it as global allocator for size-sensitive widgets. Skip it if you alloc heavily or need speed.

quiz.explain: wee_alloc is optimized for code size over throughput.

takeaway: Use wee_alloc when every kilobyte counts.
trap: Using it for alloc-heavy workloads tanks performance.

body_md: Lazy-load WASM in WebViews only when needed. Show shell UI, `import()` the module on interaction, and cache in IndexedDB. Keeps cold start under budget on low-end Android.
hook: Do not pay for WASM until the tap.

quiz.explain: Dynamic import defers fetch+compile until used.
quiz.q: How do you keep WebView startup fast with WASM?

takeaway: Defer WASM load until the feature is requested.

body_md: Set a size budget: e.g. 150KB gzipped for widget, 500KB for editor. Track `wasm-pack` output in CI with `ls` and `gzip -c | wc -c`. Fail builds that regress beyond 5%.
code:
gzip -c pkg/app_bg.wasm | wc -c
# budget check in CI
test $(gzip -c pkg/app_bg.wasm | wc -c) -lt 153600
hook: Budgets beat diets — enforce them in CI.

quiz.explain: Gzip size predicts transfer cost; CI gates regressions.
options: Gate wasm gzip size in CI
quiz.q: How do you enforce WASM size budgets?

takeaway: Measure gzipped bytes and fail on regressions.
trap: Checking raw size while serving brotli in production.

body_md: Split features behind dynamic imports and feature flags. Ship core editor now, load image codecs later. wasm-bindgen `weakRefs` plus Vite code-splitting keeps initial fetch lean.
hook: Ship half now, half on demand.

options: Split wasm by feature with dynamic import
quiz.q: How do you split large WASM apps?

takeaway: Partition by route or capability for faster first paint.

body_md: Serve `.wasm` as `application/wasm` with long immutable cache plus `Cross-Origin` headers if threaded. Preload critical modules with `<link rel=preload as=fetch>` and streaming compile.
code:
<link rel="preload" as="fetch" crossorigin href="/pkg/app_bg.wasm" />
<!-- server: Content-Type: application/wasm -->

quiz.explain: Correct MIME enables streaming compile; caching avoids refetch.

body_md: Strip symbols and debug sections for release: `wasm-strip` plus `RUSTFLAGS=-s` and LTO. Keep a separate debuginfo artifact for crashes, not in the shipped bundle.

quiz.explain: LTO plus strip removes dead code and symbols.
options: Enable LTO and strip symbols for release
quiz.q: How do you shrink release WASM builds?

takeaway: Optimize and strip release profiles aggressively.
trap: Stripping before you can symbolize field crashes.

body_md: Measure with browser perf panel and `performance.now()` around init and frames. Track compile time vs run time separately. A 50ms compile plus 5ms frames beats 500ms compile with 3ms frames.

quiz.explain: Separating phases shows whether to optimize size or hot loops.
options: Time init vs frame cost separately
quiz.q: How do you profile WASM startup?

trap: Optimizing hot loops when startup dominates bounce rate.

body_md: Fallback to JS if WASM fails: feature-detect `WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming`, catch init errors, and load pure-JS path. Log failures to know when fallback actually triggers.
code:
try { await init(); runWasm(); }
catch (e) { console.warn(e); runJsFallback(); }

quiz.explain: Graceful fallback keeps app working on old WebViews.
options: Try wasm then fallback to JS on error
quiz.q: How do you handle WASM load failure?

takeaway: Always ship a JS fallback for hostile networks.
trap: Assuming all WebViews support SIMD or threads.
